heading: \completeness.of.reals
proof_text:
In the axiomatic characterization of $\mathbb{R}$ as an abstract
ordered field tuple $(R, 0, 1, +, \cdot, \leq)$, the Least Upper Bound
property is directly stipulated: for every nonempty subset
$A \subseteq R$ bounded above by $M \in R$, there exists a unique
minimal upper bound $s = \sup(A) \in R$.

Concretely, in the Dedekind cut realization, a real number is a cut
$D \subsetneq \mathbb{Q}$. If $\mathcal{S}$ is a nonempty set of
Dedekind cuts bounded above by a cut $M$, their union
$D_{\sup} = \bigcup_{D \in \mathcal{S}} D$ is itself a Dedekind cut:
1. $D_{\sup} \neq \emptyset$ because some $D \in \mathcal{S}$ is
   nonempty; and $D_{\sup} \subseteq M \subsetneq \mathbb{Q}$, so
   $D_{\sup} \neq \mathbb{Q}$.
2. If $p \in D_{\sup}$ and $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ with $q < p$, then
   $p \in D$ for some $D \in \mathcal{S}$. Since $D$ is a cut,
   $q \in D \subseteq D_{\sup}$ (downward closure).
3. If $p \in D_{\sup}$, then $p \in D$ for some $D \in \mathcal{S}$,
   so there is $r \in D \subseteq D_{\sup}$ with $r > p$ (no maximal
   element). Thus $D_{\sup}$ is a valid Dedekind cut that contains
   every $D \in \mathcal{S}$ and is contained in any other upper
   bound, establishing that $D_{\sup} = \sup(\mathcal{S})$.

[\completeness.of.reals]
Theorem:
given: S \:(nonempty)::subset:/ \reals
where:
. exists: M is \real
  suchThat:
  . forAll: x is \real
    where: x "in" S
    then: x \:real.leq?:/ M
then:
. exists: sup is \real
  suchThat: sup = \real.supremum:of{S}
Documented:
. called: "Completeness of the Real Numbers"
. description: "Every nonempty set of real numbers bounded above has a least
                upper bound in $\mathbb{R}$."
